summary: Implemented an opt-in, backend-issued authorization/catalog seam inside the existing SQL investigator. Dynamic schema discovery and restricted execution are demonstrated with small fixtures, including a previously unknown published reference dataset. This is NOT completion of the requested enterprise research capability: real Console identity binding, approved data policies, live publication coverage, semantic discovery/accreditation and real adaptive research remain pending.

ownership.scope: MODULE_LOCAL: Telchi exploratory_sql and this phase's report only
ownership.existing_changes: Large preexisting tracked/untracked worktree preserved; exploratory_sql itself was already untracked. Git diff does not expose its preexisting baseline. Only the four explicitly listed existing files were edited; two Python files were added.
ownership.shared_components: Console/Auth, Foundation producers/readers, Messaging, Web, PostgreSQL migrations and global resource guard were read-only dependencies; no edits
ownership.git_operations: Read-only branch/status/diff checks; no add, commit, push, checkout or other mutating Git operations

implemented: EffectiveScope is backend-owned identity, organization, workspace, effective permissions and active state; never read from model JSON.

console_scope calls existing PermissionConsoleRepository.list_effective_permissions after the consuming backend's live identity/organization/workspace validator. It does not expand role names or FULL_ACCESS itself.

SourcePolicy binds an already-approved permission to an organization/workspace/source and optional column projection. No default policies, registered permissions, grants, role seeds or production configuration were introduced.

Only whole-dataset policies are supported; partial row policies withhold the entire dataset. Whole-dataset means explicitly approved business access to all rows in that source, not a grant inferred from technical FULL_ACCESS.

ResearchBinding intersects effective permissions, tenant/workspace and server policy before issuing the catalog. Validator accepts only the actual issued context object, not a by-value copy or caller-edited catalog.

Live resolver checks occur on authorization, each query validation/execution, view preparation, after execution, before sending observations to Luna, after Luna returns, and before presentation/final save.

Revocation or identity/workspace changes deny access; backend authorization failure denies rather than using cached permissions. Conversation history and protected report results are scrubbed on revoked session presentation.
Binding.close invalidates execution and evidence presentation. The binding is process-local; there is no persisted investigation resume implementation.

Read-only Foundation attachment and exact publication/snapshot equality are checked before creating private authorized projections. Model SQL only reaches those projected logical tables through the existing AST validator.
authorization.real_integration_limit: The existing Console resolver is async while the DEV executor authorization port is synchronous. A real backend-owned worker/async bridge and a concrete existing live identity validator are still required. The CLI has NO new login or authenticated Console mode, and remains explicitly supervised-local-uid by default. No actual Presidencia, Abraham or FULL_ACCESS account was impersonated or queried.
authorization.policy_limit: Changing an approved source/column policy requires closing/reissuing the binding. Dynamic revocation tests cover current identity/effective permission changes, not a persistent policy-version service. No new business grants are approved by this implementation.
authorization.audit: Reuses investigation reports, context/query digests and result evidence. No new durable Console audit event or database audit integration was implemented.

algorithm: open_binding performs the existing host read preflight, resolves the selected publication using FoundationReader, and obtains server-approved source names from current effective scope and policies.
Enumerates the selected manifest's components/datasets plus FoundationReader's existing contract map. It does not add a new hand-maintained investigator table/column catalog.
Discovers reference dataset directories inside that publication's immutable reference version, then uses access.reference(dataset). Arbitrary host paths are never model inputs.

Uses existing access.relation(component,dataset), or product_semantics_relation for the existing semantics component. Unsupported contracts become explicit gaps, not guessed physical paths or direct HANA reads.

DESCRIBE obtains actual column names, SQL types and nullability. Only safe identifiers and supported scalar types are exposed. The open_binding path filters unauthorized sources before schema queries and gap reporting.
Intersects discovered columns with approved column policy; physical relations/paths remain private to the binding and are omitted from the model catalog.

Unknown grain, relationships, currency, units, temporal coverage and business semantics remain explicitly unaccredited. No source identifiers are automatically equated with final buyers, historical classifications, net billing or collections.
dynamic_discovery.central_design_test: test_new_reference_dataset_discovered_without_catalog_entry writes a tiny fixture Parquet for previously_unknown_domain, discovers it and its novel_identifier/new_measure columns through metadata, and builds an authorized catalog without changing any investigator table list.
dynamic_discovery.not_complete: This is dynamic structural discovery, not the complete semantic discovery requested. It does not yet import accredited grain, known relationships, coverage, monetary/unit definitions or domain classifications from all available contracts. The default local ask catalog is intentionally unchanged; only Session(authorized_binding=...) uses the new catalog.

sql_and_verification.retained: Existing model gpt-5.6-luna, medium reasoning, no fallback; same adaptive controller, AST regeneration, execution lock, deadline/cancellation, query budgets, FoundationReader and independent verifier. No capability for a specific question was added.
sql_and_verification.composition_change: For issued phase-B contexts only, a validated LIMIT on a derived SELECT/CTE provides a proven output cardinality bound. This enables bounded equijoins without increasing max_join_pairs=10000. A LIMIT outside an oversized join cannot bypass its earlier check. Unbounded joins remain rejected.
sql_and_verification.rejection_feedback: A phase-B join_pair_budget denial is returned as structured observations plus REFORMULATE guidance instead of closing the entire investigation. No larger budget or alternate physical access is granted. Legacy behavior is unchanged.
sql_and_verification.verification_limit: Existing AskRegistry is preserved. Discovered tables deliberately have no accredited grain; their apparent arithmetic cannot be promoted to verified business claims. ask_verifier now explicitly refuses such accreditation with discovered_grain_and_business_semantics_not_accredited. Generic numeric/semantic verification for dynamically discovered sources is NOT implemented.
sql_and_verification.business_answer_first: Existing verified partial-result rendering remains in place. This phase does not produce a newly accredited business answer over the generic authorized catalog; doing so requires real semantic contracts and an independent general verifier. SQL success alone is not reported as business accreditation.
sql_and_verification.os_security: DEV only, not an OS sandbox. No product-grade filesystem/network isolation or enforced process RSS/CPU/scan-byte limit is claimed.

Corrected initial fixture run: 19 passed in 78.07s
Final hardening targeted run: 3 passed, 24 deselected in 11.03s

differences_from_free_pi: Luna still chooses SQL and subsequent research steps, but can only query backend-issued source/column projections and pinned publication/snapshot.
No shell, arbitrary host files, arbitrary SQL functions, physical references, external connections or model-selected authority.
Derived LIMIT joins are possible within the same budget; large joins and unsupported AST remain restricted, not yet parity with free Pi.
Only independently verified structured claims may be delivered as accredited; unknown business semantics cannot be inferred from successful SQL.
Default terminal remains supervised local DEV, not Console Presidencia or real FULL_ACCESS.
risks_and_next_steps: Do not deploy, configure business grants or freeze for phase C from this report.
Have Mario approve concrete permission-to-source/column/full-row contracts using existing permissions; no broad source policy is enabled by default.
Connect the existing authenticated backend's identity/workspace validation and fresh Console effective-permission resolution to the synchronous DEV execution port without a second login system.
Replace dependence on the reader's private _COMPONENT_TABLES map when Foundation offers a public inventory contract; no Foundation change was made here.

Add and validate rich semantic metadata and a generic independently reconciled verifier before expecting accredited business answers from new dynamic sources. Current conservative discovered-grain refusal is intentional, not task completion.

After host stability and normal service preflight, inspect actual publication coverage and run raw materials plus an unrelated model-chosen investigation, preserving complete observations and verification traces.
Rerun live revocation/evidence ownership and broader V1 regressions, then reconsider phase-C readiness.
